celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is, declare your Lord free of what is not befitting Him; «اسم» is redundant (zāʾid). ﴿الْأَعْلَى﴾: a ṣifa (adjective) of «ربك».

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى﴾ what He created: He made it proportioned in its parts, without disparity,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ﴾ what He willed ﴿فَهَدَى﴾ to what He decreed of good and evil,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعَى﴾: caused the herbage to grow,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾, after the greenness, ﴿غُثَاءً﴾: dry, crumbled stubble, ﴿أَحْوَى﴾: black and withered.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ﴾ the Qur'an ﴿فَلَا تَنْسَى﴾ what you recite,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ that you forget, through the abrogation of its recitation and its ruling. He ﷺ used to recite aloud along with Jibrīl's recitation for fear of forgetting, so it is as if it were said to him: Do not hasten with it; you will not forget, so do not tire yourself by reciting it aloud. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ — He, Exalted is He — ﴿يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ﴾ of speech and action ﴿وَمَا يَخْفَى﴾ of both.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى﴾: for the easy law, which is Islam.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾: admonish with the Qur'an ﴿إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَى﴾ — from the reminding of the one mentioned in «سيذكر» — meaning: and even if it does not benefit; it benefits some, and does not benefit some others.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿سَيَذَّكَّرُ﴾ by it ﴿مَنْ يَخْشَى﴾: fears Allah the Exalted, like the verse {فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ}.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا﴾, that is, the reminder, that is, he leaves it aside and pays no attention to it — ﴿الْأَشْقَى﴾, in the sense of «الشقي» ("the wretched one"), that is, the disbeliever,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرَى﴾: it is the Fire of the Hereafter, and the lesser one is the fire of this world.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا﴾ so as to find rest ﴿وَلَا يَحْيَى﴾ a pleasant life.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ﴾: has succeeded ﴿مَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾: purified himself through faith

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ﴾ saying "Allahu akbar" ﴿فَصَلَّى﴾ the five prayers. That is among the matters of the Hereafter, and the disbelievers of Mecca turn away from it.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ﴾ — with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] [تُؤْثِرُونَ] — ﴿الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ over the Hereafter,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾, that is, the success of the one who purifies himself and the Hereafter being better, ﴿لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى﴾, that is, those revealed before the Qur'an,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى﴾: these are ten scrolls for Ibrāhīm, and the Torah for Mūsā.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبِّحِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾: اسم is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ربك; ﴿الْأَعْلَى﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ربك; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾: conjoined to خلق.

daas-irab:3-3.t: The clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: The clause is also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾: a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿غُثاءً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَحْوى﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا تَنْسى﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of reason, لا is negative, and an imperfect verb whose agent is latent.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the excepted; ﴿شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْجَهْرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾: a relative noun conjoined to الجهر; ﴿يَخْفى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَنُيَسِّرُكَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لِلْيُسْرى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿نَفَعَتِ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾: agent; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿سَيَذَّكَّرُ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَخْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:11-11.t:
[Translator's note: the Arabic source text of this entry is garbled (the brackets and opening letters of the quoted words are lost: «َ يَتَجَنَّبُهَا»», «لْأَشْقَى»»); the quoted words are restored from the verse وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى.]
﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿الْأَشْقَى﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of الأشقى; ﴿يَصْلَى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿النَّارَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾: adjective of النار; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَمُوتُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿وَلا﴾: negative; ﴿يَحْيى﴾: conjoined to يموت.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أَفْلَحَ﴾: a past verb; ﴿مَنْ﴾: its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَزَكَّى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَذَكَرَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿اسْمَ رَبِّهِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ربه; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَصَلَّى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and صلى is conjoined to ذكر.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿تُؤْثِرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and أبقى is conjoined to the khabar.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَفِي الصُّحُفِ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and في الصحف is the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الْأُولى﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿صُحُفِ﴾: badal (substitute) for الصحف; ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَمُوسى﴾: conjoined to إبراهيم.

dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غُثاءً) In the Qāmūs: "al-ghuthāʾ, like ghurāb and like zinnār: rubbish, foam, and the perished, worn-out leaves of trees." It also says: "al-qamsh is the plural of qumāsh, which is the scraps of things on the face of the earth, so that the dregs of people are called qumāsh, and 'he gave me nothing but qumāsh', i.e. the poorest thing he found." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ghuthāʾ al-sayl is what the flood carries; ghathā al-wādī, ghuthūwan (of the pattern qaʿada), means the valley became full of ghuthāʾ; and ghathat nafsuhu, taghthā, ghathyan (of the pattern ramā) and ghathayānan is its turbulence, so that one is nearly sick, from a mixture flowing into the mouth of the stomach."
(أَحْوى) al-aḥwā is of the pattern afʿal from al-ḥuwwa, which is a blackness tending to greenness; it is also said that al-aḥwā is greenness with blackness upon it; al-aḥwā is also the gazelle, because it has two lines on its back; one says "a man aḥwā" and "a woman ḥawwāʾ", and its plural is ḥuwwun, like aḥmar and ḥumr. In the Qāmūs: "al-ḥuwwa, with ḍamma, is blackness toward greenness, or redness toward blackness; ḥawiya, like raḍiya, ḥawan." Ibn Jinnī said: al-ḥuwwa is a redness tending to blackness that occurs in the lip, and the Arabs find that desirable. Dhū l-Rumma said:
لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس ... وفي اللّثات وفي أنيابها شنب
صفراء في نعج بيضاء في دعج ... كأنها فضة قد مسّها ذهب
(A slender-lipped girl, in whose lips is a dark ruddiness, a deep red, and in her gums and in her teeth a cool sweetness; yellow-tinged in her fair whiteness, white against the dark of her eyes, as if she were silver that gold has touched.)
And Abū ʿUbayda recited, also from Dhū l-Rumma, about the pasture that is aḥwā:
حوّاء قرحاء أشراطيّة وكفت ... فيها الذهاب وحفتها البراعيم
(A dark-green, white-blazed pasture of the Ashrāṭ star, on which the light rains dripped, and the buds surrounded it.)
al-qarḥāʾ is the white one; one says "qarḥa" of a blaze (ghurra); ashrāṭiyya means rained on by the star-setting of the two Sharaṭān; al-dhihāb, with kasra on the dhāl, is light rain; and al-barāʿīm is the plural of burʿūma, which is the flower before it opens, and it is also called the kamm, the plural being aknām.

* I'rab:
(سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى) سبّح is an imperative verb, meaning "declare transcendent", and has been treated before; its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and اسم ربك is its direct object. Al-Jalāl made it an interpolated word, on the model of Labīd's saying:
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما ... ومن يبك حولا كاملا فقد اعتذر
(Until the year, then the name of peace be upon you both; and whoever weeps a full year has made his excuse.)
There is no need for this strained reading, since declaring transcendent may fall upon the name, i.e. declare the name of your Lord transcendent above being used to name an idol or image, so that it is called "lord" or "god". And الأعلى is an adjective of ربك; Ibn Hishām allowed it to be an adjective of اسم. (الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى) الذي is a second adjective of the Lord; the clause خلق is the ṣila (relative clause), and the object of خلق is omitted, i.e. "everything"; the فاء is a conjunction, and سوّى is conjoined to خلق. What is meant by "proportioning" is that He created what He willed in the most complete and perfect manner, according to an order described as firm and masterly, free of blemishes and defects. (وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدى) This too is conjoined, in sequence, to what preceded. (وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أَحْوى)
This too is conjoined to what precedes it; the clause أخرج is the ṣila of الذي, and المرعى is the direct object; فجعله is conjoined to أخرج, the هاء is the first direct object, غثاء is the second direct object, and أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. But a difficulty arises, since al-ghuthāʾ is the dry matter while al-ḥuwwa is a lasting greenness, so the two contradict each other. It is therefore preferable to parse أحوى as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى, i.e. "He brought it forth aḥwā, black from the intensity of greenness, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought it out of the pasture black from the intensity of greenness and abundant watering, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As for His saying, the Exalted, أحوى, it is said that it is an adjective of غثاء, and it is said that it is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture green and then turned it into ghuthāʾ, so he put part of the ṣila first." Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent sense is that أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. Ibn ʿAbbās said the meaning is: He made it dark ghuthāʾ, i.e. black, because when ghuthāʾ ages and rain strikes it, it blackens and rots and becomes aḥwā. It is also said that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture aḥwā, i.e. black from the intensity of its greenness and freshness through abundant watering; and the postposing of أحوى is good for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). He said:
وغيث من الوسمي حوّ تلاعه ... تبطنته بشيظم صلّتان
(And a rain from the wasmī season, whose hollows are dark-green, I entered it on a long-legged, lean, swift horse.)"
Ibn Khālawayh said in his book "I'rab of Thirty Surahs of the Noble Qur'an": "فجعله غثاء أحوى means that Allah made the pasture aḥwā, and al-aḥwā is intensely green, tending to black because of abundant watering, and then He turned it into ghuthāʾ after it dried; so the meaning involves a fronting and postponing." Ibn Hishām said in his book al-Mughnī, in mentioning the aspects from which an objection may enter against the one who parses: "The fourteenth is the saying of some about أحوى that it is an adjective of غثاء. This is not correct without qualification; it is so only if aḥwā is interpreted as black from dryness and withering. But if it is interpreted as black from the intensity of greenness through abundant watering, as مُدْهَامَّتَانِ was interpreted, then making it an adjective of غثاء is like making قيما an adjective of عوجا; rather it must be a ḥāl from المرعى, postposed to match the verse-endings." By my life, he has settled the dispute in what he laid down. (سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى) The سين is a particle of futurity; نقرئك is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; and تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative. The wording of Abū l-Suʿūd: "سنقرئك فلا تنسى is an exposition of Allah the Exalted's special guidance of His Messenger ﷺ following the exposition of His general guidance of all His creatures, namely his, peace be upon him, guidance to receive the revelation, to memorize the Qur'an, and his guidance of all people. The سين is either for emphasis or because what is meant is making him recite what Allah revealed to him at that time and what would be revealed to him afterwards, so it is a promise that the revelation will continue within the promise of making him recite, i.e. We shall make you recite what We reveal to you, and what follows, through the tongue of Jibrīl, or We shall make you a reciter by inspiring recitation, so you will not forget at all, from the firmness of memorization and mastery, even though you are unlettered, not knowing what writing or reading is; so that is another sign for you, besides what lies within what you recite of the clear signs, in respect of inimitability and of informing about the unseen." The فاء is a conjunction and لا is negative: Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet that he would not forget. تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative sign being the implied ḍamma on the alif. It is also said that لا is prohibitive and تنسى is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its jussive sign being the dropping of the weak letter, and then the alif was brought as a support for the fatḥa of the sīn so as to agree with the verse-endings, as in His saying السبيلا. Abū Ḥayyān did well when he condemned this view; he said: "This is a weak statement; the sense of the verse is utterly clear, and they have been far-fetched in understanding it." (إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَما يَخْفى) إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is the object of تنسى; the exception is vacated (mufarragh) from the most general of objects; the clause شاء الله is the ṣila of ما; and the clause إن and what is within its scope is a justification of what precedes; إن and its noun; the clause يعلم is its predicate; and الجهر is a direct object;
the واو is a conjunction and ما is a relative noun conjoined to الجهر; the clause يخفى is its ṣila. Al-Samīn said: "It is not permissible for it to be maṣdar-forming, lest the verb be left without an agent; were it not for that, its being maṣdar-forming would be better, so that an interpreted maṣdar would be conjoined to a plain maṣdar like it." (وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرى فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرى) The واو is a conjunction; ونيسرك is conjoined to سنقرئك; it is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; and ولليسرى are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to نيسرك, i.e. to the tolerant Islamic law. The فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know that you are among those who receive perfecting outpourings through Our guidance and success, then remind"; إن is conditional; نفعت is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and الذكرى is the agent. In إن there is a sense of regarding it as improbable, as though he were sure they would not incline to guidance and would persist in riding the back of excess. The apodosis (jawāb) of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes. Al-Zamakhsharī has a subtle question and a subtler answer. He said: "If you say: the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to remind whether the reminder benefits or not, so what is the meaning of making benefit a condition? I say: it has two aspects. One is that the Messenger of Allah had already exhausted his effort in reminding them, and they only increased in insolence and tyranny from the increase of reminding, and the Prophet ﷺ was burning with regret and anguish and increasing in grief and eagerness over reminding them; so it was said to him: 'You are not a compeller over them' — so remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat, and turn away from them and say 'Peace', and remind if the reminder benefits, and that is after the argument has been established by repeated reminding. The second is that it is conditional in form, but its meaning is a censure of those who remind, a report of their state, a regarding as improbable that the reminder will affect them, and a recording against them that their hearts are sealed, as you say to the preacher, 'Enrage the tax-collectors, if they listen to you,' intending by this condition to regard that as improbable and that it will never be." As for Ibn Khālawayh, after citing the view we cited he said: "Others say: إن means قد, i.e. remind, for the reminder has benefited; but that is very remote, and supposition and speculation do not befit the style of the Qur'an." As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said:
"The apparent sense is that his command to remind is conditional on the reminder's benefit, and this condition was brought only as a rebuke to Quraysh, i.e. if the reminder benefits these tyrannical, obstinate ones, and its meaning is the improbability of their benefiting from the reminder. It is as the poet said:
لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حيّا ... ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي
(You have made yourself heard, had you called one alive; but there is no life in him whom you call.)
Al-Farrāʾ, al-Naḥḥās, al-Zahrāwī and al-Jurjānī said: its meaning is 'and if it does not benefit', so he limited himself to the one alternative because it indicates the other." (سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى، وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى، الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرى، ثُمَّ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها وَلا يَحْيى) The سين is a particle of futurity; يذكر is an imperfect verb, nominative; من is a relative noun, the agent; the clause يخشى is a ṣila with no grammatical position; ويتجنبها is conjoined to سيذكّر; the هاء is a direct object and the pronoun refers back to الذكرى; and الأشقى is the agent. Ibn Khālawayh said: "One says 'Zayd is al-ashqā' and 'the woman is al-shaqyā', like al-aʿlā and al-ʿulyā, and one says: 'al-ashqā spoke to al-shaqyā', 'the two ashqayn spoke to the two shaqyayn', 'the ashqūn spoke to the ashqayn', and 'the shaqiyyāt spoke to the shaqiyyāt'." الذي is an adjective of الأشقى; the clause يصلّى has no position because it is the ṣila of الذي; the agent of يصلّى is a latent pronoun referring to الأشقى; النار is a direct object and الكبرى is an adjective of النار; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; لا is negative; يموت is an imperfect verb, nominative; وفيها are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يموت; and ولا يحيا is conjoined to لا يموت. The meaning of the delay is that wavering between life and death is more terrible than burning, so it is delayed from it in degrees of severity: "he who dies is at rest"; but these are neither dead, that they might rest, nor alive, that they might find a breath from the punishment. (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى) قد is a particle of affirmation; أفلح is a past verb; من is the agent; the clause تزكى, i.e. purified himself, has no position because it is the ṣila of من; وذكر is conjoined to تزكى; واسم ربه is a direct object; and فصلّى is conjoined to ذكر. (بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى) It is an iḍrāb (turning away) from an implied statement to which the speech leads, the implied form being: "you do not do what is for the good of your affair, rather you prefer"; تؤثرون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the واو is the agent; الحياة is a direct object and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. What is meant by preferring the life of this world is inclining to it, being deceived by its adornments, and seeking out its milk-flows. The واو is a ḥāl-wāw; الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); and أبقى is conjoined to خير; so in it are the pleasures of this world and what the mind cannot conceive of increase upon them, and it has besides that the attribute of permanence and eternity. (إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى) إن is a particle resembling the verb; هذا is its noun, the demonstrative referring to the success of him who purified himself and the words that followed; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في الصحف is the predicate of إن; الأولى is an adjective of الصحف; and صحف إبراهيم وموسى is a badal (substitute) for الصحف.

* Benefits:
A glimpse of the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā:
In al-Khāzin the following is reported: From Abū Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mosque has a greeting." I said: "And what is its greeting, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Two rakʿas that you pray." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah revealed to you anything of what was in the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā?" He said: "O Abū Dharr, recite: قد أفلح من تزكّى وذكر اسم ربه فصلّى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Mūsā?" He said: "They were all lessons: 'I wonder at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice; I wonder at one who is certain of the Fire, how he can laugh; I wonder at one who sees the world and how it turns with its people, how he can feel at ease with it; I wonder at one who is certain of destiny, and then is angry; I wonder at one who is certain of the reckoning, and then does not act.'"
In al-Qurṭubī the following is reported: "Al-Ājurrī narrated from Abū Dharr, who said: I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Ibrāhīm?' He said: 'They were all parables: O king, empowered, tried, deluded: I did not send you to heap up the world one part upon another, but I sent you to repel from Me the plea of the wronged, for I do not reject it, even were it from the mouth of an unbeliever.' And in them were parables: 'It is for the wise person to have an hour in which he converses privately with his Lord, an hour in which he reflects on the handiwork of Allah, mighty and majestic, and an hour in which he is alone for his needs of food and drink. And it is for the wise person to covet only three things: provision for the return, a means for livelihood, and a pleasure in what is not forbidden. And it is for the wise person to be discerning of his time, attending to his own affair, guarding his tongue; and whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds, his speech is little except in what concerns him.'"

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾, and ﴿باسم ربك﴾.
Both of these have occurred, and it is of the speech of the Arabs.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ﴾.
He determined His creation, and guided the male of the beasts to the way of approaching the female.
It is also said: He determined and guided and led astray; so mention of guidance sufficed for mention of misguidance, because of how often it accompanies it. The readers are agreed on the doubled form (قدّر). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī used to read قَدَر, lightened, and they consider it to be from the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah have mercy on him) [135/a]. The doubled form is dearer to me because the readers agree on it.

farraa:5-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أَحْوَىٰ﴾.
When vegetation becomes dry, it is غثاء (stubble). الأحوى: what has turned black from age. It may also be: He brought forth the pasture dark green (أحوى), then made it stubble; so it is placed later while its meaning is earlier.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلاَ تَنسَىٰ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
He did not will that he should forget anything. It is like His saying: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّماوَاتُ والأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّك﴾, and He does not will [otherwise]. You would say in speech: "I will surely give you all that you ask, except what I will" and "unless I will to deny you", while the intention is not to deny him. On this pattern run the oaths in which an exception is made, while the swearer's intention is fulfilment.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَشْقَى﴾.
He avoids the reminder and does not take heed.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾.
It is the lowest of the layers of the Fire.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ﴾.
He did good and gave charity. It is also said: قد أفلح من تزكى: he gave charity before going out on the day of the Eid.

farraa:15-15.t:
﴿وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ﴾.
He attended the prayer with the imam.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
The readers agreed on the tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy it is: "بَلْ أَنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ", a confirmation for whoever [«لم» in the source, read «لمن»] read with tāʾ.
Some readers read: "بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ".

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِي ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
He says: whoever mentions the name of his Lord and prays and does good — that is in the former scriptures just as it is in the Qurʾān.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (والذي قدر فهدى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is conjoined to the preceding relative noun.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «غثاء» is a second object; «أحوى»: naʿt (adjective) of «غثاء», accusative (manṣūb).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «سنقرئك» is resumptive; the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause «فلا تنسى» is conjoined to the clause «سنقرئك»; and «لا» is negating, with no governing effect.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «إلا» is a particle of exception; «ما»: a relative noun, the excepted; the clause «إنه يعلم» is resumptive; «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to «الجهر».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «ونيسِّرك» is conjoined to the clause {سَنُقْرِئُكَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «فذكّر» is resumptive, and the conditional clause is resumptive; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: (ويتجنبها الأشقى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the resumptive one before it.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (الذي يصلى النار الكبرى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (قد أفلح من تزكى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «وذكِّر» is conjoined to the clause {تَزَكَّى}.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (والآخرة خير وأبقى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and «خير»: an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) whose hamza was dropped for lightness

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying, the Exalted: (فجعله غثاء أحوى): the hāʾ and (غثاء) are two objects of (جعل), because it means "made into" (صيّر). (أحوى) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الغثاء), meaning "black". It is also said that (أحوى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المرعى), (أحوى) meaning "green", i.e. He brought out its greenness and then made it stubble. (الغثاء) is dry, broken plant matter, like the scum of a flood.

mekki-muskil:6-7.t:
His saying (فلا تنسى): (لا) has the meaning of (ليس); it is a statement, not a prohibition, since it is not permissible for a person to be forbidden from forgetting, because it is not by his choice.
His saying (إلا ما شاء الله): (ما) is in the position of the accusative as an exception, i.e. "you will not forget except what Allah wills to lift its recitation and abrogate it without replacement". It is also said that (تنسى) means "you leave", so the meaning is "except what Allah wills to command you to leave, so you leave it". It is also said that its meaning is "except what Allah wills, and Allah does not will that you forget any of it"; so it is like His saying in Hūd, in the two places: (خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك); it is said that its meaning is "except what your Lord wills, and He, exalted be His mention, does not will to leave off any of the eternity", since His will for them of eternity has preceded. There are many views on it other than this, which we have set out separately and explained in a separate book. It is also said that (إلا ما شاء الله) is an exception from (فجعله غثاء أحوى).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿سبح﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿أنت﴾.
﴿اسم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الأعلى﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ربك﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); or an adjective of ﴿اسم﴾, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive as a second adjective (ṣifa) of al-rabb.
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿خلق﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The object of khalaqa is omitted, i.e. "kulla shayʾ" (everything).
﴿فسوى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and sawwā is a past verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿خلق﴾, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿والذي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and alladhī is a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿الذي﴾ in the previous ayah.
﴿قدر﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾. The clause ﴿قدر﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The object of qaddara is omitted, i.e. "kulla shayʾ" (everything).
﴿فهدى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and hadā is a past verb conjoined to ﴿قدر﴾, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿والذي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and alladhī is a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿الذي خلق﴾.
﴿أخرج﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾. The clause ﴿أخرج﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿المرعى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فجعله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; jaʿala is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿غثاء﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿أحوى﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿غثاء﴾, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-marʿā, accusative by an implied fatḥa, i.e. He brought it forth dark green (aḥwā), black from the intensity of its greenness, then made it stubble after its dark greenness.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿سنقرئك﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position; nuqriʾuka is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu"; and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ﴿لا﴾ is negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿تنسى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as the object of ﴿تنسى﴾; the exception is emptied (mufarragh), from the most general of objects.
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿شاء الله﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of ﴿إن﴾. The clause of inna and what falls within its scope is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of what precedes it.
﴿يعلم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿يعلم﴾ is khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿الجهر﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and mā is a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-jahr, in the position of the accusative.
﴿يخفى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif. The clause ﴿يخفى﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ونيسرك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; nuyassiruka: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Nuyassiruka is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سنقرئك﴾.
﴿لليسرى﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and al-yusrā is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نيسرك﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿فذكر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and dhakkir is an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿إن﴾: conditional, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿نفعت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الذكرى﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿سيذكر﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and yadhdhakkar is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿يخشى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. The clause ﴿يخشى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ويتجنبها﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سيذكّر﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the pronoun refers to ﴿الذكرى﴾.
﴿الأشقى﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الأشقى﴾.
﴿يصلى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. The clause ﴿يصلى﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the fāʿil (agent) of yaṣlā is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿النار﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿الكبرى﴾: a naʿt of ﴿النار﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the implied fatḥa, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿لا﴾: negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يموت﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يموت﴾.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ﴿لا﴾ is negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يحيا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿لا يموت﴾; it is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿قد﴾: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿أفلح﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿تزكى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur). The clause ﴿تزكى﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿وذكر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and dhakara is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿تزكى﴾; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿اسم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ربه﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فصلى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ṣallā is a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, conjoined to ﴿ذكر﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿بل﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿تؤثرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿الحياة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿الدنيا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الحياة﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿والآخرة﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and al-ākhira is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿خير﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿وأبقى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and abqā is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿خير﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿لفي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) is a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and fī is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الصحف﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الأولى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الصحف﴾, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma [Translator's note: so in the source; as a naʿt of the genitive ﴿الصحف﴾ it would be genitive by an implied kasra].

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿صحف﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿الصحف﴾ in the previous ayah, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿إبراهيم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote.
﴿وموسى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and mūsā is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ibrāhīm, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra [Translator's note: so in the source; mūsā is normally treated as a diptote, whose genitive would be an implied fatḥa].

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: سبّح اسم ربك and سبّح باسم ربّك are both correct. Abū Jaʿfar said: If he reckoned this on the basis of omitting the bāʾ, then [it fails, since] مررت زيدا is not permissible; and if he reckoned it as one of those verbs that pass on [to their object] with and without a particle, so that the meaning is one, it is not so, because the meaning of سبّح باسم ربّك is "let your glorification be by the name of your Lord". The scholars have spoken about the meaning of سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى with answers all of which differ from the meaning of [the phrase] that has the bāʾ. Some of them said: its meaning is "declare the name of your Lord, the Most High, transcendent, and exalt it above your attributing to Him what the polytheists attributed to Him", because He is الأعلى, i.e. the One who subdues everything, i.e. who is high above it. Some of them said: i.e. do not say al-ʿUzzā, because it is derived from العزيز, nor al-Lāt, because they derived it from their saying الله. Some of them said: the meaning of سبّح اسم ربّك is "mention the name of your Lord while you are magnifying Him, humble and submissive". And some of them said its meaning is "glorify the name of your Lord in your prayer, humbly, occupied with it". Abū Jaʿfar said: The first answer is the clearest of them, as was read [in transmission] to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ: Isrāʾīl narrated to us from Abū Isḥāq, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ recited سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى (1), he would say: سبحان ربي الأعلى ("Glory be to my Lord, the Most High").
الْأَعْلَى is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ربك, or of اسم; it is preferable that it be a naʿt of what [the vowel] indicates. [Translator's note: the closing phrase «لما عليه» is obscure in the source; since الأعلى shows no case vowel, the sense may be that it should qualify the noun whose position it agrees with.]

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: [سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى refers to] Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. He said:

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: He said: [وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى refers to] ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Umayya ibn Khalaf.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: He said: [النَّارَ الْكُبْرى is] Hell. Al-Farrāʾ said: the lowest of the layers of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
There are several views on its meaning. It was said: the souls of the people of the Fire are in their throats; they do not come out so that they might die, nor return to their places in their bodies so that they might live. It was also said: they do not die so as to find rest, nor live a life from which they benefit. It was also said: it is from the saying of the Arabs, when someone is in severe hardship, "he is neither alive nor dead", as the poet said: [al-khafīf] 559-
ليس من مات فاستراح بميت ... إنّما الميت ميّت الأحياء
(The one who died and found rest is not [truly] dead; the dead one is only the dead among the living.)

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
There are two views on its meaning. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى:] whoever purified himself of polytheism, i.e. became pure. Al-Ḥasan said: مَن تزكى is one whose deeds were pure. The other view is from Qatāda, who said:
مَن تزكّى [is one who] paid the zakāt of his wealth.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ means he affirmed that He is] One. He said: فَصَلَّى — he is saying: then he performed the five prayers. Someone else said: صلّى here means "he supplicated". The correct view according to Muḥammad ibn Jarīr is that the meaning is "he prayed, and mentioned the name of his Lord in his prayer with praise and glorification". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake according to the view of the Arabic scholars, because he put what is before the fāʾ after it, and this is the reverse of what the grammarians have said. The correct view is that of Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: [بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ:] if you wish, you assimilate the lām into the tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy: «بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا»; this is a reading by way of explanation. Abū ʿAmr read «بل يؤثرون» with yāʾ, on the basis that it refers back to الأشقى.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى (18): there are three views on its meaning. One of them is that His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, "and the Hereafter is better and more lasting" is in the former scriptures; this seems to be the school of Qatāda. It was also said: [the statement that] success belongs to whoever purifies himself, mentions the name of his Lord and prays is in the former scriptures. The third view is that by it is meant the surah, as was read [in transmission] to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ, from Sharīk, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: سبّح اسم ربّك الأعلى is from the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā. Allah knows best what He intended; but the view of Qatāda is good because it refers to what immediately precedes it, and the way of a thing is that it refers to what is next to it, unless a decisive proof comes that changes that.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: [صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى is genitive] as a badal (substitute). الصحيفة is the written book.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
الَّذِي خَلَقَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الأعلى, or, if you wish, of ربك. It is permissible to qualify an adjective, because in meaning it is the thing qualified; on this basis يا يزيد الكريم ذو الجمّة ("O noble Yazīd with the long locks") is permissible. The meaning of الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى is "who created the creatures and proportioned their form, so that all of it became good in what was made".
وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ, i.e. He determined their forms, their provisions and their deeds. فَهَدى: it was said: so He made clear to them. It was also said: the meaning is "so He guided and led astray". It was also said: so He guided them to their interests.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى is] in the position of the genitive, conjoined. المرعى is what the beasts eat.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: [غُثاءً أَحْوى are] two objects. There are two views about it. One of them: "and who brought out the pasture, dark (أحوى), i.e. green verging on black, then made it stubble". The other view: "and who brought out the pasture and then made it black stubble". This is nearer to correctness; fronting and postponing [of words] only occurs when the meaning cannot be sound otherwise — especially since Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فجعله غثاء أحوى — he is saying: dry, withered and changed.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: There are two views about it. One of them: "so you will not leave [it]". The other is that it is from forgetting (النسيان). This is preferable, because the exegetes hold it. Mujāhid said: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite to himself so as not to forget. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb said: Mālik ibn Anas narrated to me concerning His saying سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى: he said: you will memorise, «except what Allah wills». The meaning in both views together is "you will not forget"; it is a statement, not a prohibition. According to the greatest of the lexicographers it is not permissible for a person to be forbidden to forget, because forgetting is not in his control.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of the accusative as the excepted. There are several views on its meaning. On the first answer: you will not leave anything of what Allah commanded you except what Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, wills that We abrogate, so that He commands you to leave it and you leave it. It was also said: you will not forget except what Allah wills you to forget, and Allah does not will that you forget any of it.
This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who likened it to His saying خالِدِينَ فِيها ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ [Hūd: 107]. It was also said: the meaning is "you will not forget except what Allah wills of what befalls human beings". It was also said: you will not forget except what Allah wills to lift up and to lift its recitation. These are four answers. A fifth answer is that the meaning is "then He made it dark stubble, except what Allah wills". Allah knows best what He intended. إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ, i.e. what is manifest and open, وَما يَخْفى, what is concealed and hidden; i.e. so do not commit acts of disobedience to Him, for He knows what is outward and what is inward.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: That is, for the easiest state.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: There are two views about it. One of them: "so remind in every case, whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit", like سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ [al-Naḥl: 81] [where the cold is understood as well]. The other answer is that the reminder benefits in every case, so the meaning is as you say: "remind, if you are doing what you were commanded".

safi-cedvel:16-17.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for transition (iḍrāb intiqālī) away from an implied statement, i.e. "you do not do that; rather you prefer ...". (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
Clause: «تؤثرون ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «الآخرة خير ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) «[Note: It may be resumptive, in which case it has no grammatical position.]».

safi-cedvel:18-19.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (في الصحف) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna. (صحف) is a badal (substitute) for الصحف, genitive.
Clause: «إنّ هذا لفي الصحف» has no grammatical position (resumptive).

* Benefits:
- Some of what was in the Scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā, peace be upon them both:
On the authority of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mosque has a greeting." I said: "And what is its greeting, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Two rakʿas that you pray." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, did Allah reveal to you anything of what was in the Scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā?" He said: "O Abū Dharr, recite: (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى. وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى. بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا. وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى.
إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى. صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the Scrolls of Mūsā?" He said: "They were all lessons: (I am amazed at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice! I am amazed at one who is certain of the Fire, how he can laugh! I am amazed at one who sees the world and its turning against its people, how he can feel at ease! I am amazed at one who is certain of the divine decree, then exhausts himself in toil! I am amazed at one who is certain of the reckoning, then does not act!)." This hadith was recorded by Razīn in his book, and Ibn al-Athīr mentioned it in his book Jāmiʿ al-Uṣūl.
And al-Nasafī cited the saying: In the Scrolls of Ibrāhīm: (The intelligent person should guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs).

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(اسم) is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative «[Note: some exegetes made the word (اسم) redundant, but there is no need for that, for declaring the Name transcendent is declaring transcendent the One who owns the Name]». (الأعلى) is an naʿt (adjective) of ربّك, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra. (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of genitive as a second naʿt of ربّك; the two relative nouns that follow are conjoined to the first, in the position of genitive. (غثاء) is a second direct object, accusative. (أحوى) is an naʿt of غثاء, accusative «[Note: the word may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى — in the view of Abū l-Baqāʾ — i.e. "He brought out the herbage black, then made it dry chaff"]».
Clause: «سبّح ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي)).
And the clause: «سوّى ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause خلق).
And the clause: «قدّر ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي)).
And the clause: «هدى ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause قدّر).
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the third relative noun (الذي)).
And the clause: «جعله ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause أخرج).

* Morphology:
(5) أحوى: an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from حوي يحوى (the pattern of فرح), meaning "to be black with a touch of green". In al-Qāmūs: الحوّة (with ḍamma) is blackness tending to green, or redness tending to black; and حوي حوى is like رضي. The wazn of أحوى is أفعل, its feminine is حوّاء and its plural is حوّ (with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and shadda on the wāw).

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) denotes the future. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is a negative particle «[Note: or, according to some, it is prohibitive, and the alif is redundant, a lengthening of the vowel of the sīn to suit the verse ending]»; the object of (تنسى) is omitted, i.e. "you will not forget what you recite". (إلّا) is for exception. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the excepted; the second (ما) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to الجهر.
Clause: «سنقرئك ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «لا تنسى ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause سنقرئك).
And the clause: «شاء الله ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما)).
And the clause: «إنّه يعلم ... » has no grammatical position (causal).
And the clause: «يعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يخفى» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (ما)).

* Morphology:
(تنسى): it contains a weakening by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); the original is تنسي with a vowelled yāʾ at the end. The yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(يخفى): it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is يخفي with a vowelled yāʾ at the end. The yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.

safi-cedvel:8-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction. (لليسرى) is attached to (نيسرك). (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition. (نفعت) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its tāʾ is vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two silent letters. (السين) denotes the future. (من) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as agent. (الذي) is in the position of nominative as an naʿt (adjective) of الأشقى. (ثمّ) is for conjunction. (لا) is negative in both places.
Clause: «نيسرك ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause نقرئك «[Note: in verse (6) of the sūra]»).
And the clause: «ذكّر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the reminder benefits the one who takes heed, then remind ...".
And the clause: «نفعت الذكرى ... » has no grammatical position (explicative of the implied protasis).
And the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
And the clause: «سيذّكر من يخشى ... » has no grammatical position (causal).
And the clause: «يخشى ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من)).
And the clause: «يتجنّبها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause سيذّكر).
And the clause: «يصلى ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative noun (الذي)).
And the clause: «لا يموت ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يصلى).
And the clause: «لا يحيا» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause لا يموت).

* Morphology:
(8) اليسرى: feminine of الأيسر, meaning "the easier"; it is an elative (ism tafḍīl) from اليسر. The wazn of اليسرى is فعلى (with ḍamma).
(10) الأشقى: an elative from الشقاء; its wazn is أفعل. It contains a weakening by substitution; the original is الأشقي, the yāʾ was vowelled with a fatḥa before it and was changed into alif.
(13) يحيا: the alif is written long because it is not a proper name and is preceded by a yāʾ; in the muṣḥaf it is written with an undotted yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) is a particle of confirmation. (من) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as agent. (الواو) is a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء).
Clause: «أفلح من تزكّى ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «تزكّى ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من)).
And the clause: «ذكر ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause of the ṣila).
And the clause: «صلّى ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause ذكر).

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الأعلى}: it may be genitive as an adjective of «ربِّك», and accusative as an adjective of «اسم». However, this rules out «الذي» being an adjective of «ربِّك»; rather it must be made an adjective of «اسم», or be cut off (maqṭūʿ), so as not to require separation between the adjective and the qualified noun by the adjective of another; for the construction would become like your saying «جاءني غلامُ هندٍ العاقلُ الحسنةِ» ("there came to me the servant of Hind, the intelligent, the beautiful (fem.)"), in which «العاقل» separates «هند» from its adjective. The discussion of annexing the name to the named has already been given.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ لاَ يَمُوتُ}: «ثم» is for the gap between ranks in severity.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr read it with the third person, and the rest with the second person; both are clear.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وأبقى}: i.e. than this world.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لَفِي الصحف}: Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of al-Aʿmash and Hārūn, read it with sukūn on the ḥāʾ in both places, and this too is clear.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {إِبْرَاهِيمَ}: the majority read it with an alif after the rāʾ and a yāʾ after the hāʾ; Abū Rajāʾ read it without them, the hāʾ with fatḥa or with kasra, so two readings are reported from him. Abū Mūsā and Ibn al-Zubayr read it with two alifs, and likewise throughout the Qur'an; Mālik ibn Dīnār read it with an alif after the rāʾ only, the hāʾ having fatḥa; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr read «وإبْرَاهيم» without the alif and with kasra on the hāʾ. Ibn Khālawayh said: "«إبْراهُم» has also been reported," meaning with an alif and ḍamma on the hāʾ. The discussion of this noble name and its dialect forms has already been given in full in al-Baqara.
[Translator's note: in the source, the closing quotation mark after Ibn Khālawayh's statement is missing.]

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {قَدَّرَ}: al-Kisāʾī read it with a light dāl; the rest read it with a doubled dāl. The two readings were given earlier in al-Mursalāt.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {غُثَآءً}: either a second object or a ḥāl. al-Ghuthāʾ, with doubled thāʾ or light, the latter being the eloquent form, / is what the torrent deposits at the sides of the valley of plants and the like. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4549 - كأنَّ ذُرا رأسِ المُجَيْمِرِ غُدوةً ... من السَّيْلِ والغُثَّاء فَلْكَةُ مِغْزَلِ
(As if the heights of the summit of al-Mujaymir at morning, with the torrent and its debris, were the whorl of a spindle.)
al-Farrāʾ transmitted it as «والأَغْثاء» in the plural; there is something unusual in it, in that he pluralised fuʿāl as afʿāl.
His saying: {أحوى}: there are two views on it, the clearer being that it is an adjective of «غُثاء». The second: that it is a ḥāl from «المَرْعَى». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He fronted part of the relative clause." I (al-Samīn) say: he means that the original is «أخرجَ المرعى أَحْوى فجعله غثاءً» ("He brought forth the pasture dark green, then made it debris"), but this is not called fronting part of the ṣila. al-Aḥwā is afʿal from al-ḥuwwa, which is a blackness tending toward greenness. Dhū l-Rumma said:
4550 - لَمْياءُ في شَفَتَيْها حَوَّةٌ لَعَسٌ ... وفي اللِّثاتِ وفي أَنْيابِها شَنَبُ
(Lamyāʾ, with a dark-red tinge on her lips, and on her gums and her teeth a cool brightness.)
You have already seen that some grammarians took this verse as evidence for the existence of badal al-ghalaṭ (substitute of mistake). It is also said: greenness with blackness upon it. al-Aḥwā is also the gazelle, because on its back are two lines. He said:
4551 - وفي الحَيِّ أَحْوَى يَنْفُضُ المَرْدَ شادِنٌ ... مُظاهِرُ سِمْطَيْ لُؤْلُؤٍ وزَبَرْجَدِ
(And in the tribe is a dark-lipped fawn, shaking the arāk-berries, wearing two strands, of pearl and of peridot.)
One says «رجلٌ أَحْوَى» and «امرأةٌ حَوَّاء», and the plural of both is «حُوٌّ», like «أحمر» and «حمراءُ» and «حُمْر».

semin-durr:6-6.t: {فَلاَ تنسى}: it is said to be a negation: the Exalted informed that His Prophet, peace be upon him, will not forget. It is also said to be a prohibition, with the alif being a lengthening; something like this was given earlier in Yūsuf and Ṭāhā. Makkī denied that it could be a prohibition because one is not forbidden what is not within his choice. This is not necessary, for the meaning is a prohibition against engaging in the causes of forgetting, and this is common.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ الله}: there are several views on it. One: that it is a complete exception (mufarragh), i.e. "except what Allah wills to make you forget, for you will forget it"; what is meant is the lifting of its recitation. In the hadith: "He used to wake up having forgotten verses," on the basis of His saying {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا} [البقرة: 106]. It is also said that the meaning of that is fewness and rarity, as it was reported that "he, peace be upon him, omitted a verse in his prayer; Ubayy supposed that it had been abrogated and asked him, and he said: 'I forgot it.'" al-Zamakhsharī said: "The aim is to negate forgetting altogether, as a man says to his companion: 'You are my partner in what I own, except what Allah wills,' not intending to except anything; and it is among the uses of fewness in the sense of negation." End of quotation. al-Farrāʾ and Makkī preceded him to this view. al-Farrāʾ and a group with him said: "This exception is a ṣila (filler) in speech following the practice of Allah the Exalted in exception; and there is no [thing] allowed to be excepted." The Shaykh said: "This ought not to occur in the speech of Allah the Exalted nor in any eloquent speech; likewise the view that «لا» is a prohibition and the alif a separator." End of quotation. What the Shaykh said was not intended by the one who called it a ṣila, i.e. purely redundant, but rather the meaning he mentioned, namely emphasis in negating forgetting or forbidding it.
Makkī said: "It is also said: the meaning of that is 'except what Allah wills', and Allah does not will that he forget anything of it, so it is like His saying in Hūd in both places: {خالِدِيْنَ فيها ما دامَتِ السماواتُ والأرضُ إلاَّ ما شاء ربُّك}, and He, exalted be His mention, did not leave out anything of the eternity because of the precedence of His will for their eternity." It is also said: it is an exception from His saying {فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أحوى}; Makkī related this. This ought not to be permitted at all.
His saying: {وَمَا يخفى}: «ما» is a noun (ismiyya). It cannot be maṣdariyya, lest the verb be left without an agent. Were it not for that, the maṣdariyya would be better, so that an interpreted maṣdar could be conjoined to a similar explicit one.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {وَنُيَسِّرُكَ}: conjoined to «سَنُقْرِئُك», so it comes within the scope of the relief (tanfīs, the future particle); and the sentence between them is parenthetical.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {إِن نَّفَعَتِ}: «إنْ» is conditional. There is in it a sense of regarding their taking heed as remote. From this:
4552 - لقد أَسْمَعْتَ لو نادَيْتَ حَيَّاً ... ولكنْ لا حياةَ لمَنْ تُنادي
(You would have made yourself heard had you called one alive; but there is no life in the one you call.)
It is also said: «إنْ» means «إذْ», as in His saying {وَأَنْتُمُ الأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ} [آل عمران: 139]. It is also said: it means «قد»; Ibn Khālawayh mentioned it, and it is very remote. It is also said: something is omitted after it, the implied form being: "whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit"; al-Farrāʾ said this, and al-Naḥḥās, al-Jurjānī and al-Zahrāwī.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى (١)).
The words of the Exalted (سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ): it is said that the word «اسْمَ» is redundant (zāʾida).
It is also said that in the speech there is an omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), i.e. «سَبِّحْ مُسَمَّى رَبِّكَ» (glorify the One named "your Lord"); Abū ʿAlī mentioned both of these in Kitāb al-Shiʿr.
It is also said that it is according to its apparent sense, i.e. keep His name exalted above debasement and lying when you swear by it.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا (١٦)).
(تُؤْثِرُونَ) is read with yāʾ, as the third person, and with tāʾ, as address; i.e. say that to them.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَاءً أَحْوَى (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (أَحْوَى): it is said that it is a naʿt (adjective) for «غُثَاءً».
It is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْمَرْعَى» (the pasture); i.e. He brought forth the pasture green, then turned it into stubble; so part of the ṣila (relative clause) was placed first.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنْسَى (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فَلَا تَنْسَى): «لَا» is negating, i.e. «فَمَا تَنْسَى» (so you will not forget).
It is also said that it is for prohibition, and it did not make [the verb] jussive (majzūm) for the sake of agreement with the verse-endings.
It is also said that the alif arises from the lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the fatḥa.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Aʿlā
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلى﴾ ("glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High"): that is, declare your Lord free of every evil, and say: ”سُبْحانَ رَبِّيَ الأعْلى“ ("Glory be to my Lord, the Most High").

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوّى﴾ ("Who created and proportioned"): He created the human being well-proportioned, made him bear witness against himself that He is his Lord, and created him upon the natural disposition (fiṭra).

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿والَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدى﴾ ("and Who determined and guided"): He guided him to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful. One of the grammarians said: [it means] "and guided and led astray", but ”وَأضَلَّ“ ("and led astray") was omitted because there is evidence for it in the discourse; He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ”يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي مَن يَشاءُ“ ("He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills").

zajjaj:4-5.t: ﴿والَّذِي أخْرَجَ المَرْعى﴾ ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوى﴾: ”أحْوى“ is in the position of the accusative (fī mawḍiʿ naṣb), a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ”اَلْمَرْعى“. The meaning is: ”اَلَّذِي أخْرَجَ المَرْعى أحْوى“ ("Who brought forth the pasture dark"), that is, He brought it forth green, tending toward ḥuwwa; and ”اَلْحُوَّةُ“ is blackness. ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوى﴾: He dried it until He turned it into dry, broken stubble, like the scum (ghuthāʾ) you see on top of floodwater.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى﴾ ﴿إلا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 7] ("We shall make you recite, and you will not forget, except what Allah wills"): Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He would give the Prophet ﷺ a sign by which his distinction would be made clear: that Gabriel, peace be upon him, descends to him with revelation while he is unlettered, neither writing a book nor reading it, and he teaches his Companions to recite and forgets nothing of that, and nothing has to be repeated to him. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نَـزَّلْنا الذِّكْرَ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 9] ("It is We who sent down the Reminder, and We are surely its guardians").

zajjaj:7-7.t: As for ﴿إلا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ ("except what Allah wills"), it was said: except what Allah wills, and then He reminds him of it afterwards; and it was said: except what Allah wills to defer of the Qur'an.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُها الأشْقى﴾: the meaning is ”يَتَجَنَّبُ الذِّكْرى الأشْقى“ ("the most wretched avoids the reminder").

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها ولا يَحْيا﴾ ("then he will neither die therein nor live"): he does not die a death by which he would find rest from the punishment, nor does he live a life with which he would find the comfort of life.

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكّى﴾: that is, he has attained lasting permanence and the triumph of bliss. The meaning of ﴿تَزَكّى﴾ is: he increased himself through fear of Allah (taqwā); and the meaning of ”اَلزّاكِي“ is "the growing, the abundant".

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ ("rather, you prefer the life of this world"). It was also read: ”بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا“ ("rather, they prefer…") with yāʾ; but tāʾ is better, because it is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb as: ”بَلْ أنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا“ ("rather, you prefer the life of this world").

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَفي الصُّحُفِ الأُولى﴾ ("this is surely in the former scriptures"): He means from His saying ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكّى﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 14] up to this place; and it was said: rather, the whole sūra.
